title: Restore gradient validation linkage in headless firmware
description:
## Context

Run pio run -e display-headless against the reviewed source with its dependencies installed. Observe undefined references to bg_library_valid and bg_map_valid in WebUIPlugin settings handling. The 8 MB environment shares the excluding CMake filter; repeat there with a writable dependency directory.

title: Calibrate load cells against acknowledged applied factors
description:
## Context
Review finding 10, snapshot 8f8ad95e. Source lines may move; locate the named functions in the current tree.

**[P2] Calibration calculates from an unsaved factor rather than the applied factor.**

   Location: [MachineTab.jsx](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/web/src/pages/Settings/tabs/MachineTab.jsx:108).

   `measuredWeight` reflects the controller's currently applied scale factor, but calibration multiplies it by the editable `formData.scaleFactorN`. Those differ after a manual edit, sign flip, or a previous calibration before Save. Example: applied factor 2500, reported 80 g, known mass 100 g gives the correct draft 2000. Re-entering 100 g and calibrating again before saving produces 1600 from the unchanged live reading. Saving that second result miscalibrates the scale.

   Calculate against the acknowledged applied factor, or perform calibration on the controller from raw readings. Prevent another calibration against a pending draft until the new factor is applied and fresh measurements arrive.

## Steps to Reproduce
Use an applied factor of 2500 and a fresh valid reading of 80 g. Enter a known 100 g mass and calibrate to get draft 2000. Before saving, re-enter 100 and calibrate again. The unchanged live reading multiplied by draft 2000 produces incorrect draft 1600. Repeat with an unsaved sign flip and with the second cell.

## Acceptance Criteria
Reported weight is paired with the factor that actually produced it; unsaved edits/sign flips/repeated calibration cannot compound the factor; applied 2500 with 80 g measured against 100 g remains draft 2000 on repeat until acknowledged; both cells and save/fresh-sample sequencing are covered.

## Evidence
Branch review: .beads/reviews/idf5-2026-09-05.md. Issue is based on the reviewed code or explicitly stated test output; verify the final changed code and record the tested revision.
acceptance_criteria: Reported weight is paired with the factor that actually produced it; unsaved edits/sign flips/repeated calibration cannot compound the factor; applied 2500 with 80 g measured against 100 g remains draft 2000 on repeat until acknowledged; both cells and save/fresh-sample sequencing are covered.

title: Recover animation startup after partial overlay allocation failure
description:
## Context
Review finding 12, snapshot 8f8ad95e. Source lines may move; locate the named functions in the current tree.

**[P2] A transient overlay allocation failure disables animation until reboot.**

   Location: [SleepAnimation.cpp](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/src/display/ui/default/SleepAnimation.cpp:1007), [allocation check](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/src/display/ui/default/SleepAnimation.cpp:1076).

   `overlayCap` is set before allocating the overlay buffers and tables. If a required allocation returns null, `start()` returns with that capacity still nonzero. Future starts skip the whole allocation block because it is guarded only by `overlayCap == 0`; `overlayOk` then fails forever, even after memory pressure has cleared. Successful partial allocations also remain held.

   Retry individual missing allocations, or roll back partial construction and reset the initialization sentinel. Fault-inject each required allocation and verify a later start can succeed.

## Steps to Reproduce
Fault-inject one required ov.buf, ov.runs, or ov.runN allocation during the first SleepAnimation::start. Restore allocator availability and call start again. overlayCap remains nonzero, so allocation is skipped and overlayOk still fails. Repeat at every required allocation and check cleanup/retained allocation ownership.

## Acceptance Criteria
Each required allocation can fail without permanently latching a nonzero capacity; partial allocation is rolled back or missing buffers are retried; subsequent start succeeds after memory recovers; retained successful allocations are not leaked or double-freed.

## Evidence
Branch review: .beads/reviews/idf5-2026-09-05.md. Issue is based on the reviewed code or explicitly stated test output; verify the final changed code and record the tested revision.
acceptance_criteria: Each required allocation can fail without permanently latching a nonzero capacity; partial allocation is rolled back or missing buffers are retried; subsequent start succeeds after memory recovers; retained successful allocations are not leaked or double-freed.

title: Retain framebuffer ownership until animation shutdown is confirmed
description:
## Context
SleepAnimation::stop waits up to 500 ms for each worker and endDirectPath only bounds its DMA drain, then proceeds even if retirement is unconfirmed. DefaultUI::stopSleepAnimation immediately enables LVGL framebuffer rendering. A worker blocked in a band or delayed DMA completion can outlive the handoff; push-task creation failure also marks stopped while the render task may still be running.

## Steps to Reproduce
In a controlled task/DMA test, hold a worker in a band-slot wait or delay DMA completion past the stop deadlines. Invoke stopSleepAnimation and observe whether LVGL gets framebuffer ownership while the worker/transfer is still live. Separately fail creation of SleepPush after SleepAnim starts. These are targeted fault-injection scenarios derived from source, not physical-device reproductions performed during review.

## Acceptance Criteria
Represent stop completion explicitly; do not return shared buffers/gates to LVGL or reuse task state while a worker/DMA can still access them; provide bounded UI responsiveness via deferred completion/quarantine; inject delayed slot/DMA retirement and push-task creation failure and verify no races, double deletion, or permanent gate loss.

title: Fix the AMOLED rectangle contract for animation band pushes
description:
## Context
Review finding 2, snapshot 8f8ad95e. Source lines may move; locate the named functions in the current tree.

**[P1] Animation band pushes can read beyond their buffers on AMOLED displays.**

   Location: [SleepAnimation.cpp](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/src/display/ui/default/SleepAnimation.cpp:1636), [Amoled_DisplayPanel.cpp](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/src/display/drivers/AmoledDisplay/Amoled_DisplayPanel.cpp:214).

   SleepAnimation passes exclusive rectangle endpoints to `pushColors(x0, y0, x1, y1, pixels)`. The AMOLED implementation interprets the last two coordinates as width and height and forwards them to `draw16bitRGBBitmap`. AMOLED exposes no direct framebuffer, so animations use this fallback. For example, a two-row band at y=100 passes a height of 102 while its allocation contains only two rows. Display clipping does not repair the source-buffer length mismatch. Cropped x coordinates introduce the corresponding width mismatch.

   Standardize the Display rectangle contract and convert endpoints to dimensions in the AMOLED adapter. Verify it with a fake panel that checks the supplied source extent and with an AMOLED device. The pre-existing adapter mismatch is newly exposed by repeated small animation bands.

## Steps to Reproduce
Using a checked fake AMOLED adapter, submit a two-row animation band at y=100 and nonzero/cropped x. Trace SleepAnimation::pushLoop passing exclusive x1/y1 into Amoled_DisplayPanel::pushColors, then draw16bitRGBBitmap receiving them as width/height. Check the requested source extent exceeds w*2 pixels. Device reproduction remains to be done on a 466x466 AMOLED panel.

## Acceptance Criteria
Display::pushColors has one explicit coordinate contract across all adapters; a checked fake panel accepts cropped and uncropped bands at nonzero x/y with no source overread; 466x466 AMOLED animation and ordinary LVGL updates are verified.

## Evidence
Branch review: .beads/reviews/idf5-2026-09-05.md. Issue is based on the reviewed code or explicitly stated test output; verify the final changed code and record the tested revision.
acceptance_criteria: Display::pushColors has one explicit coordinate contract across all adapters; a checked fake panel accepts cropped and uncropped bands at nonzero x/y with no source overread; 466x466 AMOLED animation and ordinary LVGL updates are verified.

title: Make allocation-failure monitoring nonblocking and allocation-free
description:
## Context
Review finding 3, snapshot 8f8ad95e. Source lines may move; locate the named functions in the current tree.

**[P1] Allocation-failure monitoring can deadlock on its own allocations.**

   Location: [memory_monitor.cpp](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/lib/ESPMemoryMonitor/src/esp_memory_monitor/memory_monitor.cpp:657), [memory_monitor.h](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/lib/ESPMemoryMonitor/src/esp_memory_monitor/memory_monitor.h:304).

   `sampleNow()` holds `_mutex` while growing history, building threshold vectors, and copying the public snapshot. The globally registered allocation-failure hook synchronously enters `handleAllocEvent()`, which takes the same non-recursive mutex with `portMAX_DELAY`. If any allocation made under that lock fails, the allocating task waits for a lock it already owns. Other allocation failures can subsequently block behind it. Failed-allocation reporting is enabled in the production configuration.

   Make this hook allocation-free and nonblocking: record a small event into preallocated storage and dispatch/log it later. Merely making the mutex recursive still leaves callback-copy allocation and reentrancy concerns. Add failure injection during a history/snapshot allocation.

## Steps to Reproduce
Enable failed-allocation events as production does. In a controlled test, inject allocation failure while sampleNow holds _mutex and grows history or copies its public snapshot. The synchronous heap hook enters handleAllocEvent and attempts xSemaphoreTake on that same non-recursive mutex. Assert the hook returns without waiting after the fix; this was source-traced, not fault-injected on a device during review.

## Acceptance Criteria
Failure reporting cannot take the monitor mutex or allocate; allocation failure during locked history/threshold/public-snapshot construction does not deadlock; reporting still records an event without recursive callback allocation.

## Evidence
Branch review: .beads/reviews/idf5-2026-09-05.md. Issue is based on the reviewed code or explicitly stated test output; verify the final changed code and record the tested revision.
acceptance_criteria: Failure reporting cannot take the monitor mutex or allocate; allocation failure during locked history/threshold/public-snapshot construction does not deadlock; reporting still records an event without recursive callback allocation.

title: Balance DMA issue accounting on rejected submissions
description:
## Context
Review finding 4, snapshot 8f8ad95e. Source lines may move; locate the named functions in the current tree.

**[P2] A rejected DMA submission decrements the issued count twice.**

   Location: [SleepAnimation.cpp](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/src/display/ui/default/SleepAnimation.cpp:3793), [fallback decrement](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/src/display/ui/default/SleepAnimation.cpp:3812).

   The submit path increments `dmaIssued`, rolls that increment back when submit fails, and then decrements it again in the shared CPU fallback. If the DMA engine is not ready, the fallback decrements without any preceding increment. After one failure, issued and completed counts no longer describe the same transfers. With everything retired, they differ by one; with one transfer still running, they can falsely compare equal. Drain checks therefore either time out unnecessarily or permit CPU fallback/cache operations before DMA has finished.

   Undo the reservation exactly once, and never decrement a reservation that was not made. Exercise a failed submit with zero and one earlier transfer outstanding, followed by a successful submit.

## Steps to Reproduce
Instrument/mock bandDma.submit or submitRows to reject one submission. Start with issued==completed, then repeat with one earlier transfer outstanding. Execute the shared fallback: one reservation is undone both immediately after submit and again at dmaErrors. Observe permanent count offset or a false equality before the outstanding transfer completes.

## Acceptance Criteria
Each reservation is rolled back once; an engine-not-ready failure does not decrement an unreserved count; failed submissions with zero/one earlier transfer followed by success preserve issued/completed counts and CPU fallback never races outstanding DMA.

## Evidence
Branch review: .beads/reviews/idf5-2026-09-05.md. Issue is based on the reviewed code or explicitly stated test output; verify the final changed code and record the tested revision.
acceptance_criteria: Each reservation is rolled back once; an engine-not-ready failure does not decrement an unreserved count; failed submissions with zero/one earlier transfer followed by success preserve issued/completed counts and CPU fallback never races outstanding DMA.

title: Wait for scanout handoff before LVGL reuses a framebuffer
description:
## Context
Review finding 5, snapshot 8f8ad95e. Source lines may move; locate the named functions in the current tree.

**[P2] LVGL reuses the previous framebuffer before scanout has switched.**

   Location: [LV_Helper.cpp](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/src/display/drivers/common/LV_Helper.cpp:288), [LilyGo_RGBPanel.cpp](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/src/display/drivers/LilyGo-T-RGB/LilyGo_RGBPanel.cpp:768).

   The final direct-mode flush calls `presentFrameBuffer()` and immediately calls `lv_disp_flush_ready()`. The panel call requests a flip; the bounce-buffer driver continues reading the old framebuffer until its frame-boundary handoff. LVGL swaps its draw buffers and writes the old one during the next `refr_sync_areas()`/render pass. The configured LVGL refresh period is 10 ms, shorter than the roughly 20–26 ms panel periods offered by the UI, so another refresh can write a still-scanned buffer. This creates a normal active-screen tearing path even with animations restricted to standby.

   Synchronize reuse with the actual framebuffer-complete event, including LVGL's direct-mode synchronization copies. SleepAnimation's `presentFrame()` already documents and waits for precisely this hardware distinction; apply an equivalent ownership guarantee to LVGL. Validate rapidly changing widgets with animations off.

## Steps to Reproduce
Disable active-screen animation, use direct double buffering and the configured 10 ms LVGL refresh period, and rapidly invalidate widgets at a 51/43/38 Hz panel rate. Trace final disp_flush -> presentFrameBuffer -> immediate lv_disp_flush_ready, followed by LVGL refr_sync_areas before the bounce framebuffer-complete event. Verify writes never target the still-scanned framebuffer after fixing; physical tearing was not measured during review.

## Acceptance Criteria
LVGL synchronization copies and rendering cannot write the buffer still being scanned; final flush completion follows actual framebuffer handoff; rapid widget changes with animations disabled remain tear-free at supported panel clocks; stop/start transitions retain ownership.

## Evidence
Branch review: .beads/reviews/idf5-2026-09-05.md. Issue is based on the reviewed code or explicitly stated test output; verify the final changed code and record the tested revision.
acceptance_criteria: LVGL synchronization copies and rendering cannot write the buffer still being scanned; final flush completion follows actual framebuffer handoff; rapid widget changes with animations disabled remain tear-free at supported panel clocks; stop/start transitions retain ownership.

title: Preserve recoverable profiles and notes when replacement fails
description:
## Context
Review finding 7, snapshot 8f8ad95e. Source lines may move; locate the named functions in the current tree.

**[P2] A failed replacement rename deletes both versions of a profile or notes file.**

   Location: [ProfileManager.cpp](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/src/display/core/ProfileManager.cpp:221), [ShotHistoryPlugin.cpp](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/src/display/plugins/ShotHistoryPlugin.cpp:682).

   The new temporary-file path protects against short writes, but removes the original before renaming the completed temporary file. If that rename fails, the error branch removes the temporary file too: neither version survives. A power cut between remove and rename leaves only `.tmp`; profile enumeration deliberately ignores it and there is no startup recovery. The comment calling it recoverable does not supply a recovery path.

   Use overwrite-rename where the filesystem supports it. For FAT, retain a backup and implement rollback/startup recovery. At minimum, preserve the completed temporary file after a failed commit. Inject rename failure after successful serialization and check that a recoverable complete version remains.

## Steps to Reproduce
Save an existing profile/notes file through a filesystem double. Allow complete temporary serialization and removal of the target, then fail rename(tmp,target). Observe cleanup also removes tmp and no complete version remains. Separately simulate power loss between target removal and rename and restart the loader.

## Acceptance Criteria
Short writes and failed rename leave at least one complete recoverable version; FAT uses rollback/startup recovery and LittleFS uses suitable atomic replacement; power interruption at each commit phase recovers deterministically; failed saves do not announce success.

title: Propagate controller installation failure to the overall OTA result
description:
## Context
Review finding 8, snapshot 8f8ad95e. Source lines may move; locate the named functions in the current tree.

**[P2] Controller installation failures still produce a successful overall OTA sequence.**

   Location: [GitHubOTA.cpp](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/lib/OTA/src/GitHubOTA.cpp:130), [ControllerOTA.cpp](/mnt/c/work/gaggimate/lib/OTA/src/ControllerOTA.cpp:391).

   Receiving the image (`0xF2`) is distinct from installing it. The new result handler logs every `0x0F` message and sets one `installResultReceived` flag, including explicit messages for insufficient space, a refused single-slot update, or `Update.end()` failure. `waitForInstallResult()` therefore treats receipt of a negative result as success, and GitHubOTA ignores even its boolean return. The display can then update itself and report completion while the controller retains its old firmware.

   Represent success, failure, and unknown separately. Propagate explicit installation failures to `PHASE_ERROR`; define a deliberate compatibility policy for older controllers that do not report a final result. This is a remaining gap in the OTA hardening, not a claim that the branch newly invented all false-success behavior.

## Steps to Reproduce
In a controlled transport test, acknowledge complete image receipt with 0xF2, then send a 0x0F result containing an explicit refusal, insufficient-space error, or Update.end error. Observe installResultReceived is set without success parsing and GitHubOTA continues after waitForInstallResult. Also test timeout and legacy peers; do not use a working machine for destructive failure injection.

## Acceptance Criteria
Receipt, install success, install failure, and unknown result are distinct; explicit controller refusals/Update.end failures stop the combined update before display flashing; PHASE_ERROR reaches the UI; timeout/legacy-controller policy is explicit and tested.

title: On-display settings screens
description:
Let the most important settings be changed on the display itself, without the web UI: a gear tile on the menu opens a settings screen with five category tiles, each category is a paged list of rows (steppers, choices, toggles, locked calibration rows, read-only status rows), visual settings change live, everything else is saved when the category is left. Agreed in the 2026-09-05 interview; the decisions below are the spec.

## Navigation
- Menu (`objects.menu_screen_new`) gains the settings gear tile (`objects.btn_settings_1`, currently hidden). Tap: settings cover opens on the menu screen.
- Settings home: five category tiles (Temperatures & timing, Display, Animation, Machine, Status) plus the exit chevron back to the menu.
- Category: title, up/down page arrows with a "page n/m" indicator, five rows per page, exit chevron back to the tiles. Sub-pages (wake-up schedule list and editor) stack on top; the exit chevron pops one level.

## Categories and rows
- Temperatures & timing: Temperature offset (locked, 1 C steps), Pressure sensor (locked, 0.1 bar steps), Brew delay (50 ms), Grind delay (50 ms), Delay auto-adjust (toggle).
- Display: Main brightness (1..16, live), Standby brightness (0..16), Dim after (standby dim timeout, 30 s steps), 24-hour clock (toggle), Time zone region (choice), City (choice).
- Animation (all live): Animation (choice by name), Frame rate (5..60, step 5), All screens (toggle), Theme (Dark/Light), Gradient (Default, built-in themes, stored library gradients, for the current animation), Plates (Keep/Hide/Custom), Plate colour (palette), Plate opacity (0..100, step 5), Element tint (toggle), Tint colour (palette), Text scrim (0..100, step 5).
- Machine: Startup mode (Standby/Brew), Standby timeout (Never, 1..240 min), Auto wake-up (toggle), Schedules (opens the list: add up to 8, each with hour and minute steppers, seven weekday toggles, remove).
- Status (read-only, refreshed every second): Display firmware, Controller firmware, Network, IP address, Controller, Scale, Time; plus Restart (hold 2 s).
- Excluded on purpose: steam pump assist, boiler fill, momentary buttons, scale source, HomeKit, Home Assistant, OTA, WiFi credentials, reset to defaults.

## Structure of the work
- gm-flw.1 value model (host-tested), .2 shell, .3 row widgets, .4 menu tile, .5 synthetic tap injection (`TouchInject` module, LVGL and SDL hooks, `/api/debug/tap`), .15 bench readouts (active-screen touchmap with label texts and debug tags, `anim_id` and `uptime_ms`, `/api/debug/synth`, `tools/touchmap.py`), .16 rig helper (`tools/settings_ui_tests/rig.py` with the simulator launcher), .6 settings debug route, .7 Temperatures & timing, .8 Display, .9 Animation, .10 Machine, .11 schedule editor, .12 Status, .13 end-to-end runner, .14 documentation.
- Dependencies: .1 has none; .2 and .5 need the simulator build (gm-bzu.9); .15 follows .5 and .2; .16 follows .5 and .15; .6 follows .2, .5, .15 and .16; .3 follows .2, .6 and .15 (its rows are verified through the debug route, the tap route and the tagged touchmap); .4 follows .2, .6 and .15 (all three edit `DefaultUI.cpp`); the categories (.7, .8, .9, .10, .12) need .1, .2, .3, .6 and .16; .11 follows .10; .13 needs every user-facing bead plus .16 and gm-bzu.9; .14 follows .13. Waves that may run in parallel touch disjoint files.
- One file per category under `src/display/ui/default/settings/`. The shell's table names five `extern const SettingsCategoryDef kCat<Name>` symbols, defined weak in `SettingsPlaceholders.cpp`; each category bead defines the strong symbol in its own file and edits no shared file, so the five category beads run in parallel without collisions, and the runner bead deletes the placeholders.
- Verification venue: the desktop simulator first (`display-sim`, the same HTTP instruments on 127.0.0.1:8080, state in `sim_data/`), the bench device second (`display-loadtest` at 192.168.1.121). Memory and frame-rate numbers are device-only.

## Shared contract (identical in every bead of this epic)

- Code-built LVGL, not EEZ Studio. The settings UI lives in `src/display/ui/default/settings/` and is built with `lv_*` calls; the runtime-built scale overlay (`DefaultUI::buildScaleScreen` in `src/display/ui/default/DefaultUI.cpp`) is the precedent for construction and for delete-event pointer cleanup. It is one full-screen cover object created as a child of `objects.menu_screen_new` when settings opens and deleted when it closes. The flow screen never changes while settings is open (`currentScreen` stays `SCREEN_ID_MENU_SCREEN_NEW`), so the animation host, plate handling and screen-change code in DefaultUI are untouched. While the cover is up, every direct child of the menu screen except `objects.status_icons` is hidden (their original visibility captured and restored on close); the flow tick keeps driving flags on the menu's individual tiles and icons, which is why parents are hidden, never individual flow-controlled children.
- Look: the current style. Text and icons in `theme_colors[eez_flow_get_selected_theme_index()][0]`, backgrounds in `theme_colors[..][1]`; fonts `lv_font_montserrat_16/18/20/24` (34 and 48 exist for large values); icons from `src/display/ui/default/eez/images.h` (`img_angle_up/down/left/right_40x40`, `img_plus_small_40x40`, `img_minus_small_40x40`, `img_check_40x40`, `img_thermometer_half_40x40`, `img_clock_40x40`, `img_settings_40x40`, `img_info_40x40`, `img_tachometer_fast_40x40`, `img_power_40x40`) recoloured with the accent, or `LV_SYMBOL_*` glyphs from the Montserrat fonts. Page title in Montserrat 24 below the status icons (which sit at y 20..40). The exit chevron is `img_angle_up_40x40` at `LV_ALIGN_CENTER` + 210 px with `lv_obj_set_ext_click_area(btn, 45)`, exactly where every other screen has it; its hit rectangle is clipped by the screen to 130x95 px and it is exempt from the size and edge rules below. No translucent plates over the animation: rows are text and icons directly on the screen background (the cover has `bg_opa` 0, so the theme background or the animation shows through, whichever the menu screen has). Every translucent pixel costs blend time per animation frame (CLAUDE.md, UI-pipeline invariants). Text that does not fit its slot is truncated with `LV_LABEL_LONG_DOT`; the row keeps the canonical value string in its own storage and the debug dump exports that (the label's buffer holds the dots, `lv_label_get_text` returns them).
- Geometry: 480x480 round panel, 0.111 mm/px. For every tappable target except the exit chevron: its effective hit rectangle (coords grown by its ext click pad, clipped by every ancestor without `LV_OBJ_FLAG_OVERFLOW_VISIBLE`; `tools/touchmap.py` and `tools/settings_ui_tests/rig.py` compute this from the dumped absolute coords, which already include any translate) is at least 56x56 px, no two hit rectangles on one page overlap, and no hit rectangle reaches within 12 px of the panel edge circle (radius 240 around 240,240). Row widgets are 320x56 px, five rows per page. Every settings object that a test must find carries a `SettingsDebugTag` (row name, role: `row`, `value`, `minus`, `plus`, `prev`, `next`, `toggle`, `action`, `confirm`, `unlock`, `page_up`, `page_down`, `exit`, `tile`, `cover`, and for role `value` a pointer to the row-owned canonical value string) in its LVGL `user_data`; the touchmap dump exports the tag, and for value tags the canonical text in full, for descendants of the cover.
- Interaction: steppers step once on `LV_EVENT_PRESSED` and once on each `LV_EVENT_LONG_PRESSED_REPEAT` (LVGL defaults: `LV_EVENT_LONG_PRESSED` 400 ms after press, then a repeat every 100 ms; no step on `LV_EVENT_CLICKED`), and report `fast` after 2 s of continuous hold, whereupon the field's `fastStep` from the model applies (there is no universal multiplier). LVGL delivers at most one `LONG_PRESSED_REPEAT` per `lv_task_handler` call and resets its repeat timestamp on each, so the number of repeats in a hold depends on the UI pass cadence (a 100 ms rerender pass yields one repeat per pass); tests assert the protocol (one step per event, none on CLICKED) and wide count windows, never an exact cadence. Holds are cancelled by `LV_EVENT_RELEASED`, `LV_EVENT_PRESS_LOST`, disabling the row, page removal and deletion; hold and progress state lives in the row object and is driven only by the events LVGL delivers to it (PRESSED, LONG_PRESSED, LONG_PRESSED_REPEAT, RELEASED, PRESS_LOST, DELETE), never by a free-standing `lv_timer` that could outlive the row. Choices show `< value >` and cycle with the arrows, wrapping at both ends, arrows repeating while held. Toggles flip on tap. Locked rows (calibration) unlock after a 1 s press on the row, consume that press until release, and relock whenever the category is left. Confirm rows (Restart, Remove schedule) act once after a 2 s hold with visible progress and cancel on release. `setEnabled(false)` disables every interactive descendant and cancels pending holds.
- Saving: visual settings apply on every change (brightness, animation, frame rate, all-screens, theme, gradient, plates, tint, scrim) and each live write is followed by `ui->markDirty()` so `DefaultUI::updateState` applies it on the next pass rather than after the 2.5 s idle rerender interval. Everything else is written to `Settings` when the category is left, by any route the UI task can see (exit chevron, standby timeout, controller mode change, brew start, any flow screen change), and never lost on those routes. A category's `commit` writes only the fields the user changed. A web UI save while a category is open does not close it: the web values land first, the shell refreshes every row the user has not touched from `Settings` on the next pass after `settings:changed`, and the user's touched fields keep their draft and win at commit (per field, last writer wins). A web-requested restart (`/api/settings` POST with `restart`) reboots from the web task at once; an uncommitted display draft is lost then, the same as a power cut, and that is accepted. `Settings` properties mark themselves dirty on `set` and `Settings::loopTask` flushes every dirty property to NVS every 5 s (a flush is one or more NVS key writes, each stalling the flash cache for a scan-out slip); live rows therefore reach flash through the periodic saver while the category is still open, deferred fields become dirty only at commit, and nothing calls an immediate save per step. Concurrency: `Settings::lock()` (a FreeRTOS recursive mutex added by the shell bead, a no-op on the simulator's single thread) serialises whole transactions: the web save's `batchUpdate`, `doSave` (periodic flush, `save(true)`, `flushNow`), a category's `enter` snapshot and `commit`, and `Controller::loopLogic`'s delay auto-adjust writes. Between transactions the rule is per field, last writer wins; readers outside a transaction (`DefaultUI::updateState`) are unchanged.
- Activity: every touch inside settings calls `controller->updateLastAction()` so the standby timeout (`Controller::loopLogic`: `now > lastAction + settings.getStandbyTimeout()`, on the logic task on the device and in the one main loop on the simulator) does not fire mid-edit.
- Memory: immutable lookup tables are `const` PODs in flash (a `const std::vector` or `String` is not); runtime drafts, strings and callback contexts are small, bounded and owned by the shell for the life of the cover; anything sizeable goes to PSRAM; settings code never touches the animation hot slab (`bganim::allocHot`). LVGL objects allocate from PSRAM through `gm_lv_malloc`, so widget count is not an internal-DRAM concern, but plain C++ allocations are, and `/api/debug/heap` (`int_free`, `dma_free`) is read with the largest page and draft open.
- Wire format of GET `/api/settings` (the oracle for what was written): `standbyTimeout` and `standbyBrightnessTimeout` are in seconds (stored in ms), `temperatureOffset` and `pressureScaling` are numeric strings, `bgAnimPlateColor` and `elementTintColor` are `#rrggbb` strings, `startupMode` is `standby` or `brew`, `autowakeupSchedules` is `HH:MM|ddddddd;...` (Mon..Sun). Scripts parse before comparing.
- Verification venue: the desktop simulator first (`pio run -e display-sim`, `SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy GM_SIM_PORT=<port> ./.pio/build/display-sim/program`, web server on `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` (8080 by default), state under `sim_data/` in the working directory; the build is repaired by gm-bzu.9), the bench device second (`display-loadtest` build at 192.168.1.121). The simulator runs the LVGL UI, Settings, the web server and the debug routes on one cooperative thread with no panel and no background animation renderer (`SleepAnimation` is a stub under `GAGGIMATE_SIM` and `updateState` skips animation and plate application): it verifies navigation, interaction, values, persistence and theme colours. Animation frame counters, the applied frame-rate cap, rendered gradients, plate pixels, memory and frame-rate numbers are device-only, and a simulator pass says nothing about the device's concurrency (TouchInject's critical section and the Settings lock are reviewed on their own merits). Build note: a new or deleted source file under `src/` needs `touch src/CMakeLists.txt` before the ESP-IDF envs pick it up (the glob has no CONFIGURE_DEPENDS); when a symbol's provenance matters, check the ELF with the toolchain's `nm` (`~/.platformio/packages/toolchain-xtensa-esp-elf/bin/xtensa-esp32s3-elf-nm`).
- Rules: never POST `/api/settings` by hand (the web UI is the only safe writer) and never print the `wifiPassword` field of GET `/api/settings`; scripts read it through a filter that drops that key. No em dashes or double hyphens in prose, comments or commit messages.

title: Build the host-tested settings value model (ranges, steps, formats, zones, schedules)
description:
Build the value model behind the on-display settings as plain C++ with no LVGL or Arduino dependency, and unit-test it natively. Every range, step, wrap rule, display format, choice list, time-zone split and wake-up schedule edit that the settings screens need is decided here once, so the screen code only wires rows to model calls and the rules are testable on the host.

## Context
- Settings fields and their storage (`src/display/core/Settings.h`): `temperatureOffset` (int, C), `pressureScaling` (float, bar, default 16.0), `brewDelay`/`grindDelay` (double, ms), `delayAdjust` (bool), `mainBrightness` (int 1..16), `standbyBrightness` (int 0..16), `standbyBrightnessTimeout` (int ms, default 60000), `standbyTimeout` (int ms, default 900000, 0 = never), `startupMode` (int, `MODE_STANDBY` 0 or `MODE_BREW` 1 from `constants.h`), `bgAnimFps` (int 5..60), `bgAnimId` (int index into the animation table), `bgAnimAllScreens` (bool), `themeMode` (int, 0 Dark, 1 Light), `bgAnimClearPlates` (0 keep, 1 hide, 2 custom), `bgAnimPlateColor` (int 0xRRGGBB), `bgAnimPlateOpacity` (0..100), `elementTintEnabled` (bool), `elementTintColor` (int 0xRRGGBB), `bgAnimScrim` (0..100), `clock24hFormat` (bool), `timezone` (String, an IANA name such as `Europe/Oslo`), `autowakeupEnabled` (bool), `autowakeupSchedules` (`std::vector<AutoWakeupSchedule>`: `String time` "HH:MM", `bool days[7]` Mon..Sun; NVS and the web UI serialise it as `HH:MM|1111100;HH:MM|0000011`).
- Animation names: `bg_animation(i).name` for `i < bg_animation_count()` (`src/display/ui/default/bganim/BgAnim.h`). Gradients: `bg_theme_count()` built-ins named by `bg_theme_name(i)`; the user library `bgAnimGradients` is `id|name|gradient;...` (up to 12 entries, `BG_GRADIENT_LIB_MAX`); the per-animation assignment `bgAnimThemeMap` is `ref;ref;...` indexed by animation id where a ref is empty (use the global `bgAnimTheme`), a built-in index, or `c<id>` for a library entry; `bg_map_valid` and `bg_library_valid` check the syntax. The web UI mirrors all of this in `web/src/config/bgAnimations.js`.
- Time zones: `src/display/core/zones.h` declares `zones_t {const char *name; const char *zones;}` (IANA name, POSIX TZ string) and a header-local `static const zones_t zones[]` of 461 entries plus `resolve_timezone(name)`. Controller.cpp and DefaultUI.cpp both include it today. Regions are the text before the first `/`: Africa 52, America 149, Antarctica 11, Arctic 1, Asia 82, Atlantic 10, Australia 12, Etc 35, Europe 60, Indian 11, Pacific 38.
- Storage clamps that the model must agree with: `Settings::setBrewDelay` and `setGrindDelay` clamp to 0..4000 ms (`Settings.cpp`); the web handler clamps `bgAnimClearPlates` to 0..2. The web UI's own input ranges are in `web/src/pages/Settings/tabs/*.jsx` (brightness 1..16 and 0..16, fps 5..60, opacity and scrim 0..100).
- `autowakeupSchedules` can hold more than 8 entries today (neither the web Add handler nor the setter caps it); a cap in the model limits adding, never importing.
- The host unit-test pattern is `[env:native_autotune]` in `platformio.ini` with `test/test_autotune_simc/` (Unity, `pio test -e native_autotune`).

## Scope
Files: `src/display/ui/default/settings/SettingsModel.h`, `src/display/ui/default/settings/SettingsModel.cpp`, `test/test_settings_model/test_settings_model.cpp`, `platformio.ini` (new `[env:native_settingsui]`), plus a header-independent accessor to the zone table (`size_t zones_count()` and `const zones_t &zones_entry(size_t)` declared in `zones.h` and defined in exactly one TU, for example a new `src/display/core/zones.cpp`), so the model never includes the table itself.

## Requirements

- Model specs: Startup mode choice {Standby, Brew}; Standby timeout Never then 1..240 min in 1 min steps (fast 10), shown "15 min" or "Never".

## Scope
Files: `src/display/ui/default/settings/CatMachine.cpp`, `src/display/ui/default/settings/CatMachine.h` (the draft struct the schedule bead edits; `CatMachine.cpp` defines `kCatMachine`), `tools/settings_ui_tests/test_machine.py`.

- All deferred: `commit` writes touched fields and triggers `settings:changed` if anything was written.
- `CatMachine.h` publishes the draft struct (`MachineDraft`: startup mode, standby timeout ms, auto wake-up flag, a `std::vector` of the model's schedule struct, and per-field touched flags including `schedulesTouched`) and a row-provider hook so the schedule bead can append its "Schedules" action row and push its pages with a pointer to this draft; `commit` writes `setAutoWakeupSchedules` (converting to `AutoWakeupSchedule`) only when `schedulesTouched`. This file never knows the editor's internals.

- [ ] `pio run -e display`, `-e display-loadtest` and `-e display-sim` succeed.

- [ ] Leaving with no change writes nothing; a web save of `standbyTimeout` while the page is open shows on the row (reconcile) and survives the pop.

title: Implement the auto wake-up schedule list and editor pages
description:

- Storage: `autowakeupSchedules` is `std::vector<AutoWakeupSchedule>` (`src/display/core/Settings.h`: `String time` "HH:MM", `bool days[7]` Mon..Sun, all seven true by default, `isDayEnabled(1..7)`), setter `setAutoWakeupSchedules(const std::vector<AutoWakeupSchedule>&)`, persisted as `HH:MM|1111100;...`. - The Machine category (`CatMachine.h`) publishes `MachineDraft` (schedules vector plus `schedulesTouched`) and a row-provider hook for appending rows; its `commit` writes the schedules only when touched.
- The shell stacks pages: `pushPage(def, ctx)`, `popPage()`, `rebuildPage()`; a pushed page enters once and commits once when removed; the exit chevron pops one level; an external leave unwinds all pages top-down; the parent's draft lives until the parent's own page is removed, so child pages edit it through the `ctx` pointer they are given.

- Editor page: title "Schedule n"; rows "Hour" (stepper 0..23 wrap), "Minute" (stepper 0..59 wrap, fast 5), seven toggles "Monday" .. "Sunday", and "Remove schedule" (confirm row, 2 s hold; disabled when it is the only schedule). Two pages.
- All edits go straight into the draft's vector and set `schedulesTouched`; the editor's and the list's `commit` do nothing more (the Machine commit persists). Editor and list contexts hold the `MachineDraft` pointer and a schedule index, never an element pointer (`getAutoWakeupSchedules()` returns the vector by value and a reconcile replaces the draft's vector). title: Implement the Status category (versions, network, links, time) and the hold-to-restart row
description:
Implement the Status category: read-only rows for the display and controller firmware versions, the network name, the IP address, the controller link, the scale, and the local time, refreshed every second, plus a Restart row that reboots the display after a 2 s hold with pending settings flushed first.

## Context
- Sources (all already used by `DefaultUI::updateSystemStatus` in `src/display/ui/default/DefaultUI.cpp`): display firmware `BUILD_GIT_VERSION` (`src/version.h`), controller firmware `controller->getSystemInfo().version`, controller link `controller->getClientController()->isConnected()`, WiFi `WiFi.status() == WL_CONNECTED` with `settings.getWifiSsid()` for the name and `WiFi.localIP().toString()` for the address ; an active config AP shows as network "GaggiMate" at 4.4.4.1, known to DefaultUI as the private member `apActive` (a read-only accessor is needed); scale `controller->getActiveScaleSourceName()` and `controller->isScaleSourceHealthy(controller->getEffectiveScaleSource())`, local time via `time()`/`localtime_r` formatted with `isClock24hFormat()` like the standby clock.
- Restart today: `WebUIPlugin::handleSettings` calls `settings->save(true)` then `ESP.restart()`. `Settings::save(true)` calls `doSave()`, which returns nothing: a failed NVS open or a failed key write is logged and left pending for the 5 s retry, so a restart right after it can lose the change. The info screen (screen 10) already shows the versions, network and IP as labels, readable through the touchmap dump; `/api/status` carries only `mode`, `tt`, `ct`. `AutoWakeupPlugin::isTimeValid` shows how the firmware decides the clock is synchronised.
- The shell calls a category's `refresh` once per second while it is visible.

Files: `src/display/ui/default/settings/CatStatus.cpp` (defines `kCatStatus`), `src/display/ui/default/DefaultUI.h` (`bool isApActive() const` accessor), `src/display/core/Settings.h` and `Settings.cpp` (`bool flushNow()`), `tools/settings_ui_tests/test_status.py`.

description:
Write the end-to-end runner for the on-display settings: one command that launches the simulator (or targets the bench device with `--host`), drives the whole feature through the synthetic tap and settings debug routes, runs every category scenario, audits every settings page's touch targets, records the animation frame rate and heap while settings is open, checks persistence across a restart, and prints a pass/fail report with timestamps.

## Context
- Venues, same HTTP instruments on both: the simulator first (`pio run -e display-sim` builds `.pio/build/display-sim/program`; `rig.Sim` launches it headless with `SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy`, web server on 127.0.0.1:8080, state in `sim_data/` under the launch directory, NVS as one JSON file per namespace at `sim_data/nvs/<namespace>.json` with the Settings namespace `controller`, string values keyed by the NVS keys in `Settings.cpp`; gm-bzu.9 restores the build), then the bench device (`display-loadtest` at 192.168.1.121, `rig.synth(0)` first so the synthetic brew lifecycle stops moving the UI).
- Shared helper `tools/settings_ui_tests/rig.py`: `Rig`, `Sim` (`restart()` relaunches with the same data directory), `tap_target`, `touchmap` (screen 0, `seq`), `find_tag`, `row_value`, `targets`, `audit(dump, exempt_roles=("exit",))`, `settings()` (never returns `wifiPassword`), wire-format helpers, `settingsui(**args)`, `heap()`, `anim()`, `fb_png(path, rects)`, `wait_until`, `log(step, **kv)`.
- Scenarios `tools/settings_ui_tests/test_<name>.py` for rig, temps, display, animation, machine, schedules, status: each exposes `run(rig, report)` (raises `AssertionError` with a message naming row and value on failure) and stays runnable alone; a scenario that only has a `main()` gains the `run` wrapper in this bead.
- Touch-target rules: every target's effective hit rectangle at least 56x56 px (tiles at least 100x100), no two overlapping on one page, none within 12 px of the panel edge circle, the exit chevron exempt (fleet convention, its ext click area is clipped by the screen). `rig.audit` implements these; `rig.targets` excludes the cover and any object covering 90 percent of the screen.
- Frame rate: `/api/debug/anim` carries `anim_frames` (the loop counter), `anim_id`, `uptime_ms`; a passive rate is the counter delta over a timed window. `C:\work\camshots\anim_fpsprobe.py` is not passive (it sends previews and changes renderer overrides) and is not used here. CLAUDE.md measuring rules: rates within one boot from device time, nothing before `uptime_ms` 90 s, compare configurations by toggling within one run, and on the device read `/api/debug/pclk` first because the stored divider can differ from the build's. On the simulator the loop runs on host CPU time, so its rate is recorded, not compared.
- Heap: `/api/debug/heap` (`int_free`, `psram_free`, `dma_free`, `dma_min`, `hot_fail`, `uptime_ms`) runs a heap walk for its largest-block figure (`WebUIPlugin.cpp`, the largest-block query is intrusive) and must not be called inside a rate window. `dma_min` is the boot-lifetime minimum, a different quantity from the minimum of the runner's samples. The first touchmap request allocates a retained 64 KB PSRAM buffer and EEZ may recreate screens, so heap comparisons hold only between the same screen and configuration after a warm-up. The simulator's heap shims do not model the device, so heap assertions are device-only and the simulator only records the numbers.
- Restoration: some stored values cannot be reached through the display's steppers (a 45 s dim timeout on the 30 s grid, a fractional delay, an off-list frame rate, a colour outside the palette) and some scenarios need data that the display cannot create (a library gradient for the Animation scenario; the library defaults empty in `Settings.h`; a 9-entry schedule list for the Schedules scenario).

## Scope
Files: `src/display/ui/default/settings/SettingsPlaceholders.cpp` (deleted: every category now defines its strong `kCat<Name>`), `tools/settings_ui_test.py` (runner), `tools/settings_ui_tests/audit_pages.py` (touch-target audit over every page), `tools/settings_ui_tests/fixtures.py` (preflight and simulator seeding), `tools/settings_ui_tests/fixtures/controller.json` (the seeded simulator settings), `tools/settings_ui_tests/README.md` (runner section).

## Requirements
- `python3 tools/settings_ui_test.py [--host 192.168.1.121] [--sim-program .pio/build/display-sim/program] [--sim-port 8080] [--only rig,temps,display,...] [--skip-restart] [--report-dir out/]`: without `--host` it launches the simulator through `Sim` in a fresh directory under the report dir seeded from `fixtures/controller.json`, and tears it down at the end; with `--host` it targets the device, calls `synth(0)` (and `synth(1)` on exit), and reads `/api/debug/pclk`, recording the divider in the report and warning when it is not 6.
- Preflight, before anything is changed: confirms the instruments answer (`/api/debug/tap`, `/api/debug/touchmap?screen=0`, `/api/debug/settingsui`); reads `settings()` and checks each scenario's starting values are representable on its steppers (dim and standby timeouts on their grids, delays in 50 ms steps within 0..4000 ms, frame rate in the list, brightness in steps, plate and tint colours in the palette, since an off-palette colour is preserved only for one visit and cannot be restored across visits, so it is unsupported for any scenario that changes that colour); checks the fixtures exist (at least one library gradient, at least one schedule). - Warm-up: opens and closes every settings page once (tiles, each category page, the schedule list, one editor), waits until `uptime_ms` is at least 90 s, then, on the device, enables All screens through the settings UI if it is off (remembering the original value for restoration), confirms `/api/debug/anim` reports the renderer active (on the menu the animation runs only with all-screens on; otherwise the route answers 409 `animation not running`), and records the baseline on the menu screen: `heap()` and a 10 s passive rate window with cap 30 confirmed through `settings()`; the animation and renderer configuration stay fixed through every page window. - Pages: for each page, opens it through `settingsui`, dumps the touchmap, audits it (size, overlap, edge distance, every `row/value` label non-empty), writes `<report-dir>/<page>.png` from `fb_png` with hit rectangles drawn, and on the device records a 5 s passive rate window with no other HTTP call inside it.

- Scenarios: runs each `run(rig, report)` in a `try/finally`; a scenario's own cleanup restores what it changed through the UI, and a restoration failure is logged as `RESTORE FAILED` with the key, expected and actual value in the report without stopping the run.

- The runner never POSTs `/api/settings` (the simulator's NVS JSON is written only before the process starts), never prints `wifiPassword`, and every value it changes is restored by driving the UI.
- README: how to build and run against the simulator, how to run against the device, how to read the report, how to add a scenario.

- [ ] `pio run -e display`, `-e display-loadtest` and `-e display-sim` build without `SettingsPlaceholders.cpp`, and `grep -rn "Row n\|weak" src/display/ui/default/settings/` finds no placeholder left.
- [ ] `python3 tools/settings_ui_test.py` passes on the simulator with the whole epic merged in under 15 minutes and writes a PNG per settings page and `report.json`; `python3 tools/settings_ui_test.py --host 192.168.1.121` passes on the bench device.
- [ ] A deliberate fault fails with a message naming the page and target or the missing instrument: a scratch build with one stepper button's click pad set to 0 fails the audit of that page; `--host` pointed at a production build fails in preflight naming `/api/debug/tap`.
- [ ] A simulator seeded with `standbyBrightnessTimeout` 45 s (edited copy of `fixtures/controller.json`) reports `UNSUPPORTED FIXTURE` for the Display scenario before any change, the other scenarios still run, and the exit code is non-zero.
- [ ] `--only status --skip-restart` runs only that scenario and the audit of its pages.
- [ ] `grep -rn wifiPassword tools/` matches only the deleting line and its comment in `rig.py`.
- [ ] `python3 -m py_compile` passes for the runner and every file under `tools/settings_ui_tests/`.

title: Extend the bench readouts: active-screen touchmap with label texts and tags, anim_id and uptime_ms, synth quiet switch, touchmap.py
description:

- `/api/debug/touchmap?screen=N[&load=1]` (`WebUIPlugin.cpp`, `DefaultUI::serviceTouchMap`) makes the UI task load screen N (1..11, the EEZ enum; the service treats 0 as "no request"), walk its object tree and write a JSON dump into a retained 64 KB PSRAM buffer that the next GET returns: per object `i`, `p` (parent index), `c` (class), `o` (index into the EEZ `objects` table or -1), `x1,y1,x2,y2` (absolute coords, which already include any translate), `e` (ext click pad), `h`, `k`, `v` (hidden, clickable, overflow visible), `n` (event callback count), `ty` (translate y, diagnostic only). `tools/touchmap.py` computes effective hit rectangles from it (it currently adds `ty` a second time, which is wrong) and draws them on the framebuffer from `/api/debug/fb?step=2`; its default flow loads each screen and ends by loading standby.

title: Build the settings shell: menu-screen cover, category tiles, paged lists, lifecycle and save-on-leave
description:
Build the settings shell: the full-screen cover on the menu screen, the category tile page, the paged list page (title, page arrows, page indicator, five row slots, exit chevron), a page stack, the category registry the category beads plug into, the debug-tag convention the test instruments read, and the lifecycle rules: open, close, save-on-leave by every route the UI task can see, web-save reconciliation, theme restyle, activity refresh, pressed-feedback re-walk. With this bead alone the shell opens to five tiles whose categories contain placeholder rows, plus a bench-only fixture category, and closes back to the menu.

## Context
- Precedent for a runtime-built overlay: `DefaultUI::buildScaleScreen` (`src/display/ui/default/DefaultUI.cpp`), a cover created as a child of `objects.grind_screen` with a delete-event callback that nulls the cached pointers. It does not reset `pressedStyledRoot`; resetting it after building controls is a new requirement here, so that `DefaultUI::applyPressedFeedback` re-walks the tree (`applyPressedRecurse` styles `lv_btn` with visible backgrounds, `lv_imgbtn`, and clickable `lv_img`; a transparent text button gets nothing from it).
- Screen changes go through `DefaultUI::changeScreen` (sets `targetScreen`) and land in `DefaultUI::handleScreenChange`, which acts only when `currentScreen != targetScreen` and then calls `eez_flow_set_screen`. Routes that change the screen while settings could be open: the standby timeout (`Controller::loopLogic` calls `activateStandby` when `now > lastAction + standbyTimeout`; the `controller:mode:change` handler in `DefaultUI` then calls `changeScreen`), any other mode change, `controller:brew:start` (status screen). A BLE disconnect only sets `waitingForController` and a rerender; a web save (`WebUIPlugin::handleSettings`) writes Settings from the async_tcp task inside `batchUpdate` (today just `callback(this)`, no lock), calls `save(true)`, triggers `settings:changed` and calls `setTargetTemp(getTargetTemp())`; it does not call `applyTheme`, which runs only inside the gated rerender block of `DefaultUI::loop` (250 ms minimum interval, `markDirty()` requests it). None of that passes through `handleScreenChange`. `Controller::updateLastAction()` is public.
- The menu screen (`create_screen_menu_screen_new`, `src/display/ui/default/eez/screens.c` from line 2879) has these direct children: `objects.new_menu_dials` (the dials widget with the standby and menu icons), an unnamed 480x480 container holding the five tiles (obtainable as `lv_obj_get_parent(objects.btn_brew_1)`), `objects.status_icons` (200x20 at y 20..40, the bluetooth/wifi/error icons whose HIDDEN flags the flow tick drives), `objects.info_btn` (centre), `objects.standby_btn` (bottom) and `objects.obj13` (a centred label the flow tick writes). `tick_screen_menu_screen_new` rewrites `btn_grind_1`'s HIDDEN flag and the status icons' flags every tick, so individual tiles must not be hidden by the shell; their parents can. An `effect_mgr` effect in `setupState` repositions the tiles whenever `grindAvailable`/`scaleMenuSwap` change and `updateSystemStatus` sets `in_menu` from `targetScreen`.
- The menu screen background is the theme colour normally and transparent while the background animation hosts it (`bgAnimAllScreens`); the cover must not paint a background of its own.
- `DefaultUI::loop` runs `serviceLayerMoves()`, `serviceUiAnimTest()`, `serviceTouchMap()` at its top inside an `#ifndef GAGGIMATE_SIM` block (the simulator compiles none of them today); the shell's per-pass service call goes after that block's `#endif`, unconditionally, or it never runs on the simulator; `rerender` is gated (`RERENDER_INTERVAL_IDLE` 2500 ms) and `markDirty()` forces the next pass to run `updateState`/`applyTheme`; `change_color_theme` (generated) recolours only the EEZ objects, never runtime-built ones. `LV_USE_USER_DATA` is on and no firmware code uses `lv_obj_t::user_data` today.
- Theme colours: `theme_colors[eez_flow_get_selected_theme_index()][0]` text/accent, `[1]` background; the element tint rewrites slot 0 when enabled.

## Scope
Files: `src/display/ui/default/settings/SettingsUI.h`, `src/display/ui/default/settings/SettingsUI.cpp`, `src/display/ui/default/settings/SettingsPlaceholders.cpp`, `src/display/ui/default/DefaultUI.h`, `src/display/ui/default/DefaultUI.cpp` (ownership, `openSettings()`/`closeSettings()`, service call, external-leave hook in `handleScreenChange`, a `settings:changed` listener, menu children hide/restore, `applyPressedFeedbackTo`, the brightness log line), `src/display/core/Settings.h` and `Settings.cpp` (`Settings::lock()`), `src/display/core/Controller.cpp` (the two delay writes in `loopLogic` under the guard, nothing else).

## Requirements
- `class SettingsUI` owned by `DefaultUI`, constructed with access to `Controller &`, `DefaultUI &` and `PluginManager &`: `open()`, `close()`, `isOpen()`, `service()` (every UI pass: 1 s refresh tick for the visible page, theme/tint restyle check, web-save reconciliation), `onExternalLeave()` (unwind every page top-down calling each `commit` once, then destroy the cover), `openCategory(int)`, `gotoPage(int)`, `popPage()`, and a read-only `State {open, depth, category, page, pages, title}` published as one struct for the debug route.
- Category registry, the contract the category beads code against (names may be refined, the shape stays), in `SettingsUI.h`:
  ```
  struct SettingsDebugTag { const char *row; const char *role; const char *text; };   // in lv_obj_t::user_data of every settings object a test must find; text is non-null only for role "value": the address of the row-owned canonical string, set once, whose contents settingsRowSetValue rewrites in place
  struct SettingsCategoryDef {
      const char *title;                 // tile caption and page title
      const lv_img_dsc_t *icon;          // 40x40 tile icon
      int  (*rowCount)(void *ctx);       // may change while a page is open (schedule list)
      void (*buildRow)(void *ctx, int index, lv_obj_t *parent, SettingsUI &ui); // creates row `index` into the 320x56 slot
      void (*enter)(void *ctx);          // once when the page is pushed: snapshot Settings into the draft, relock rows
      void (*refresh)(void *ctx);        // once per second while visible, may be nullptr
      void (*commit)(void *ctx);         // exactly once when the page is removed, by any route
      void (*reconcile)(void *ctx);      // after a web save: re-read untouched fields from Settings, may be nullptr
      void *(*createCtx)();              // the category's draft, allocated by the shell at open(); nullptr for a stateless category
      void (*destroyCtx)(void *ctx);     // freed after the last commit
  };
  extern const SettingsCategoryDef kCatTemps, kCatDisplay, kCatAnimation, kCatMachine, kCatStatus;
  ```
  plus `pushPage(const SettingsCategoryDef *, void *ctx)`, `popPage()`, `rebuildPage()` (row count or row content changed), `rowsPerPage() == 5`, `kRowW = 320`, `kRowH = 56`, and helpers `Controller &controller()`, `DefaultUI &ui()`, `PluginManager &plugins()`. Lifecycle rules: a pushed page enters once and commits once when removed; paging and being uncovered by a popped child never call `enter` or `commit`; a category owns its draft until its own page is removed (a child page edits the parent's draft through the `ctx` the parent passed); `ctx` objects are owned by the shell for the life of the cover (allocated at `open`, freed after the last `commit`), so a category never stores pointers into LVGL objects across a page rebuild.
- Debug tags: every tile, arrow, chevron, row object, value label and control created by the shell carries a `SettingsDebugTag` with a stable row name and one of the roles `row`, `value`, `minus`, `plus`, `prev`, `next`, `toggle`, `action`, `confirm`, `unlock`, `page_up`, `page_down`, `exit`, `tile`, `cover`; `SettingsUI::cover()` returns the cover object (or nullptr) so the touchmap dump can restrict tag export to its descendants.
- Tile page: five category tiles (icon 40x40 over a Montserrat 16 caption) arranged on a circle around the centre, plus the exit chevron at CENTER + 210 closing settings. Each tile's effective hit rectangle is at least 96x96 px, no two overlap, none overlaps the chevron's 130x95 clipped hit box, none within 12 px of the panel edge circle; radius, tile size and pads are the implementer's to choose within those rules. A sixth "Fixture" tile exists only in `GM_TOUCH_PROBE` and `GAGGIMATE_SIM` builds (see below).
- List page: title (Montserrat 24, below the status icons), page indicator "2/3" (Montserrat 16) with up and down page arrows (`img_angle_up_40x40`/`img_angle_down_40x40`, hit pad so each is at least 56x56), hidden or disabled at the ends; five row slots 320x56 stacked and centred; exit chevron at CENTER + 210. Paging rebuilds the five rows from `buildRow`; a page change keeps the category's draft (rows are views, the draft lives in the category).
- Lifecycle: `open()` captures the visibility of every direct child of `objects.menu_screen_new`, hides all of them except `objects.status_icons`, creates the cover (transparent, `LV_OBJ_FLAG_CLICKABLE` so nothing beneath receives touches), sets `pressedStyledRoot = nullptr` once; `close()` restores the captured visibility and deletes the cover. `pushPage`, `popPage` and `rebuildPage` style the widgets they create through a new public `DefaultUI::applyPressedFeedbackTo(lv_obj_t *root)` (the existing `applyPressedRecurse` on that subtree): `applyPressedFeedback` itself re-walks the whole screen only when `lv_scr_act() != pressedStyledRoot`, the active screen never changes while settings is open, and resetting the root on every page turn would re-walk the entire menu tree per tap. Leaving a page by chevron calls its `commit` then pops. `handleScreenChange` calls `onExternalLeave()` before `eez_flow_set_screen` whenever settings is open, so the standby timeout, a mode change or a brew start never loses a pending edit and never leaves a stale cover. A delete event on the cover nulls every cached pointer. `open()` while already open is a no-op.
- Web-save reconciliation: `DefaultUI` listens for `settings:changed` (fired from the web task) and sets a `std::atomic<bool>`; the shell's `service()` consumes it with an exchange, calls the open pages' `reconcile` (untouched fields re-read from Settings, rows rebuilt) on the UI task, and calls `markDirty()` so the next pass runs `updateState`/`applyTheme` for whatever the web changed. Web values are never applied by the shell itself and the user's touched fields keep their draft. Each consumed flag logs `SettingsUI: reconcile` once.
- Theme restyle: `service()` compares the theme index and the resolved accent colour (`theme_colors[idx][0]`) with the values the current page was built with and rebuilds the page when they differ, preserving drafts, locks and holds (a held button is released by the rebuild, which is acceptable). The comparison sees the new theme only after `applyTheme` has run in the rerender pass, which the reconciliation's `markDirty()` requests; a web theme change therefore lands within one rerender pass plus one service pass.
- `Settings::lock()`: a FreeRTOS recursive mutex in `Settings` (`xSemaphoreCreateRecursiveMutex`, RAII guard `Settings::Guard`), a no-op under `GAGGIMATE_SIM` (the simulator's FreeRTOS shim has no semaphores and one thread). `batchUpdate` and `doSave` take it; the shell takes it around every page's `enter` and `commit`; this bead also wraps the two delay auto-adjust writes in `Controller::loopLogic` (`setBrewDelay`/`setGrindDelay` after a shot) in a `Settings::Guard`, so no category bead has to edit `Controller.cpp` for it. It serialises transactions, nothing more: `Property::get` stays lock-free for the UI task's readers.
- `DefaultUI::setBrightness` logs `Display: brightness %d` at info level (the Display category's tests read it on both venues; the inline body in `DefaultUI.h` moves to the .cpp).
- Every press inside the cover calls `controller->updateLastAction()` (one `LV_EVENT_PRESSED` handler on the cover with event bubbling enabled on its descendants, or one per control).
- No plates: the cover, tiles, rows and arrows have `bg_opa` 0; only text, icons and optionally a 1 px separator line per row.
- Placeholder categories: the shell's category table in `SettingsUI.cpp` lists the five `extern const SettingsCategoryDef` symbols above in the epic's order (plus the Fixture); `SettingsPlaceholders.cpp` defines each of them `__attribute__((weak))` with five placeholder rows (label "Row n") so navigation is testable before the category beads land. A category bead defines the strong symbol in its own `Cat<Name>.cpp` and edits neither `SettingsUI.cpp` nor `SettingsPlaceholders.cpp`, so the five category beads never touch a shared file; the runner bead deletes `SettingsPlaceholders.cpp` once all five strong definitions exist.
- Fixture category (`GM_TOUCH_PROBE` and `GAGGIMATE_SIM` builds only): title "Fixture", 11 rows (three pages), each an info row until the row-widget bead replaces them with one of each widget kind; `enter` increments an enter counter, `commit` a commit counter, and the draft holds one integer the row-widget bead's stepper will edit; the counters and draft value are exposed through `SettingsUI::fixtureCounters()` for the debug route and logged at info level as `SettingsFixture: enter=%d commit=%d draft=%d`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `pio run -e display`, `pio run -e display-loadtest` and `pio run -e display-sim` succeed; the production RAM figure grows by at most 512 B over the previous commit.
- [ ] With `SettingsUI::open()` invoked from a debug hook (the debug-route bead adds `/api/debug/settingsui`; until then a temporary call from the touchmap request path is acceptable and removed before commit): on the simulator (`--screenshot`, or the SDL window) the tile page shows five tiles (six on the sim/loadtest build) plus the chevron; on the loadtest device `tools/touchmap.py --screens 5` lists every tile with hit rectangles of at least 96x96 px and the arrows at least 56x56, none overlapping, none within 12 px of the edge circle except the chevron. Tag export is verified by the touchmap bead, not here.
- [ ] Opening a category shows its title, "1/n" and five placeholder rows; the page arrows change the indicator and rows; the chevron returns to the tiles; a second chevron returns to the menu with every menu child's visibility exactly as captured and `tools/touchmap.py --screens 5` identical to its pre-settings output.
- [ ] Fixture lifecycle: opening the Fixture category and paging through all three pages, then popping, logs `enter=1 commit=1`; opening it and forcing a screen change (standby timeout set to 1 min on the web UI beforehand, or a brew start on the sim's mock controller) logs `commit=1` for that visit, the cover is gone on the new screen, and the menu children are restored when the menu is next shown.
- [ ] Web-save reconciliation: with a placeholder or fixture page open, saving any setting on the web UI does not close the page and does not crash; the `settings:changed` flag is consumed on the next UI pass (log line `SettingsUI: reconcile`) on both venues (the simulator proves `service()` runs there).
- [ ] Theme restyle: switching the theme on the web UI while a page is open recolours every settings label and icon to the new accent within 500 ms on a steady screen (device framebuffer sample at a label's pixels; sim screenshot).
- [ ] `Settings::lock()`: a web save (`batchUpdate`) and a category commit forced to overlap on the device (the Fixture's commit made to spin 200 ms under the lock in a scratch build) never interleave: the `SettingsFixture: commit` line and the web save's log lines are strictly ordered, and the build without the scratch delay behaves the same.
- [ ] Every touch on the cover updates `lastAction`: with the standby timeout at 1 min, tapping a page arrow every 30 s for 3 min keeps the machine out of standby.
- [ ] Leak check on the device: after a 90 s warm-up, on the menu screen with the same animation and settings, open and close settings 50 times through the debug hook; `int_free` and `psram_free` on `/api/debug/heap` end within 1 KB and 16 KB of their pre-loop values and the loadtest serial line `GM_LVMEM: live=... n=...` shows `n` back at its pre-loop value.

## Tests
- The simulator checks above, then the device checks; scripted with the instruments as they land, manual where they have not.
- Unit: none (LVGL glue).

## Out of scope
Real rows (row-widget bead), category content, the menu tile (menu-tile bead), the debug route.
## Shared contract (identical in every bead of this epic)

- Code-built LVGL, not EEZ Studio. The settings UI lives in `src/display/ui/default/settings/` and is built with `lv_*` calls; the runtime-built scale overlay (`DefaultUI::buildScaleScreen` in `src/display/ui/default/DefaultUI.cpp`) is the precedent for construction and for delete-event pointer cleanup. It is one full-screen cover object created as a child of `objects.menu_screen_new` when settings opens and deleted when it closes. The flow screen never changes while settings is open (`currentScreen` stays `SCREEN_ID_MENU_SCREEN_NEW`), so the animation host, plate handling and screen-change code in DefaultUI are untouched. While the cover is up, every direct child of the menu screen except `objects.status_icons` is hidden (their original visibility captured and restored on close); the flow tick keeps driving flags on the menu's individual tiles and icons, which is why parents are hidden, never individual flow-controlled children.
- Look: the current style. Text and icons in `theme_colors[eez_flow_get_selected_theme_index()][0]`, backgrounds in `theme_colors[..][1]`; fonts `lv_font_montserrat_16/18/20/24` (34 and 48 exist for large values); icons from `src/display/ui/default/eez/images.h` (`img_angle_up/down/left/right_40x40`, `img_plus_small_40x40`, `img_minus_small_40x40`, `img_check_40x40`, `img_thermometer_half_40x40`, `img_clock_40x40`, `img_settings_40x40`, `img_info_40x40`, `img_tachometer_fast_40x40`, `img_power_40x40`) recoloured with the accent, or `LV_SYMBOL_*` glyphs from the Montserrat fonts. Page title in Montserrat 24 below the status icons (which sit at y 20..40). The exit chevron is `img_angle_up_40x40` at `LV_ALIGN_CENTER` + 210 px with `lv_obj_set_ext_click_area(btn, 45)`, exactly where every other screen has it; its hit rectangle is clipped by the screen to 130x95 px and it is exempt from the size and edge rules below. No translucent plates over the animation: rows are text and icons directly on the screen background (the cover has `bg_opa` 0, so the theme background or the animation shows through, whichever the menu screen has). Every translucent pixel costs blend time per animation frame (CLAUDE.md, UI-pipeline invariants). Text that does not fit its slot is truncated with `LV_LABEL_LONG_DOT`; the row keeps the canonical value string in its own storage and the debug dump exports that (the label's buffer holds the dots, `lv_label_get_text` returns them).
- Geometry: 480x480 round panel, 0.111 mm/px. For every tappable target except the exit chevron: its effective hit rectangle (coords grown by its ext click pad, clipped by every ancestor without `LV_OBJ_FLAG_OVERFLOW_VISIBLE`; `tools/touchmap.py` and `tools/settings_ui_tests/rig.py` compute this from the dumped absolute coords, which already include any translate) is at least 56x56 px, no two hit rectangles on one page overlap, and no hit rectangle reaches within 12 px of the panel edge circle (radius 240 around 240,240). Row widgets are 320x56 px, five rows per page. Every settings object that a test must find carries a `SettingsDebugTag` (row name, role: `row`, `value`, `minus`, `plus`, `prev`, `next`, `toggle`, `action`, `confirm`, `unlock`, `page_up`, `page_down`, `exit`, `tile`, `cover`, and for role `value` a pointer to the row-owned canonical value string) in its LVGL `user_data`; the touchmap dump exports the tag, and for value tags the canonical text in full, for descendants of the cover.
- Interaction: steppers step once on `LV_EVENT_PRESSED` and once on each `LV_EVENT_LONG_PRESSED_REPEAT` (LVGL defaults: `LV_EVENT_LONG_PRESSED` 400 ms after press, then a repeat every 100 ms; no step on `LV_EVENT_CLICKED`), and report `fast` after 2 s of continuous hold, whereupon the field's `fastStep` from the model applies (there is no universal multiplier). LVGL delivers at most one `LONG_PRESSED_REPEAT` per `lv_task_handler` call and resets its repeat timestamp on each, so the number of repeats in a hold depends on the UI pass cadence (a 100 ms rerender pass yields one repeat per pass); tests assert the protocol (one step per event, none on CLICKED) and wide count windows, never an exact cadence. Holds are cancelled by `LV_EVENT_RELEASED`, `LV_EVENT_PRESS_LOST`, disabling the row, page removal and deletion; hold and progress state lives in the row object and is driven only by the events LVGL delivers to it (PRESSED, LONG_PRESSED, LONG_PRESSED_REPEAT, RELEASED, PRESS_LOST, DELETE), never by a free-standing `lv_timer` that could outlive the row. Choices show `< value >` and cycle with the arrows, wrapping at both ends, arrows repeating while held. Toggles flip on tap. Locked rows (calibration) unlock after a 1 s press on the row, consume that press until release, and relock whenever the category is left. Confirm rows (Restart, Remove schedule) act once after a 2 s hold with visible progress and cancel on release. `setEnabled(false)` disables every interactive descendant and cancels pending holds.
- Saving: visual settings apply on every change (brightness, animation, frame rate, all-screens, theme, gradient, plates, tint, scrim) and each live write is followed by `ui->markDirty()` so `DefaultUI::updateState` applies it on the next pass rather than after the 2.5 s idle rerender interval. Everything else is written to `Settings` when the category is left, by any route the UI task can see (exit chevron, standby timeout, controller mode change, brew start, any flow screen change), and never lost on those routes. A category's `commit` writes only the fields the user changed. A web UI save while a category is open does not close it: the web values land first, the shell refreshes every row the user has not touched from `Settings` on the next pass after `settings:changed`, and the user's touched fields keep their draft and win at commit (per field, last writer wins). A web-requested restart (`/api/settings` POST with `restart`) reboots from the web task at once; an uncommitted display draft is lost then, the same as a power cut, and that is accepted. `Settings` properties mark themselves dirty on `set` and `Settings::loopTask` flushes every dirty property to NVS every 5 s (a flush is one or more NVS key writes, each stalling the flash cache for a scan-out slip); live rows therefore reach flash through the periodic saver while the category is still open, deferred fields become dirty only at commit, and nothing calls an immediate save per step. Concurrency: `Settings::lock()` (a FreeRTOS recursive mutex added by the shell bead, a no-op on the simulator's single thread) serialises whole transactions: the web save's `batchUpdate`, `doSave` (periodic flush, `save(true)`, `flushNow`), a category's `enter` snapshot and `commit`, and `Controller::loopLogic`'s delay auto-adjust writes. Between transactions the rule is per field, last writer wins; readers outside a transaction (`DefaultUI::updateState`) are unchanged.
- Activity: every touch inside settings calls `controller->updateLastAction()` so the standby timeout (`Controller::loopLogic`: `now > lastAction + settings.getStandbyTimeout()`, on the logic task on the device and in the one main loop on the simulator) does not fire mid-edit.
- Memory: immutable lookup tables are `const` PODs in flash (a `const std::vector` or `String` is not); runtime drafts, strings and callback contexts are small, bounded and owned by the shell for the life of the cover; anything sizeable goes to PSRAM; settings code never touches the animation hot slab (`bganim::allocHot`). LVGL objects allocate from PSRAM through `gm_lv_malloc`, so widget count is not an internal-DRAM concern, but plain C++ allocations are, and `/api/debug/heap` (`int_free`, `dma_free`) is read with the largest page and draft open.
- Wire format of GET `/api/settings` (the oracle for what was written): `standbyTimeout` and `standbyBrightnessTimeout` are in seconds (stored in ms), `temperatureOffset` and `pressureScaling` are numeric strings, `bgAnimPlateColor` and `elementTintColor` are `#rrggbb` strings, `startupMode` is `standby` or `brew`, `autowakeupSchedules` is `HH:MM|ddddddd;...` (Mon..Sun). Scripts parse before comparing.
- Verification venue: the desktop simulator first (`pio run -e display-sim`, `SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy GM_SIM_PORT=<port> ./.pio/build/display-sim/program`, web server on `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` (8080 by default), state under `sim_data/` in the working directory; the build is repaired by gm-bzu.9), the bench device second (`display-loadtest` build at 192.168.1.121). The simulator runs the LVGL UI, Settings, the web server and the debug routes on one cooperative thread with no panel and no background animation renderer (`SleepAnimation` is a stub under `GAGGIMATE_SIM` and `updateState` skips animation and plate application): it verifies navigation, interaction, values, persistence and theme colours. Animation frame counters, the applied frame-rate cap, rendered gradients, plate pixels, memory and frame-rate numbers are device-only, and a simulator pass says nothing about the device's concurrency (TouchInject's critical section and the Settings lock are reviewed on their own merits). Build note: a new or deleted source file under `src/` needs `touch src/CMakeLists.txt` before the ESP-IDF envs pick it up (the glob has no CONFIGURE_DEPENDS); when a symbol's provenance matters, check the ELF with the toolchain's `nm` (`~/.platformio/packages/toolchain-xtensa-esp-elf/bin/xtensa-esp32s3-elf-nm`).
- Rules: never POST `/api/settings` by hand (the web UI is the only safe writer) and never print the `wifiPassword` field of GET `/api/settings`; scripts read it through a filter that drops that key. No em dashes or double hyphens in prose, comments or commit messages.
