title: Build the settings row widgets: stepper, choice, toggle, locked, confirm and info rows
description:
Build the seven row widgets every settings category is made of, as LVGL objects sized for the shell's 320x56 slots: stepper, choice, toggle, action, locked (hold to unlock), confirm (hold to act) and info. Fill the shell's bench-only Fixture category with one of each so they can be exercised and measured before any real category exists.

## Context
- The shell (`src/display/ui/default/settings/SettingsUI.h`) creates rows through a category's `buildRow(ctx, index, parent, ui)` into a 320x56 parent slot, exposes `kRowW`/`kRowH`, defines `SettingsDebugTag {row, role}` (stored in `lv_obj_t::user_data`, roles `row`, `value`, `minus`, `plus`, `prev`, `next`, `toggle`, `action`, `confirm`, `unlock`) and owns a `GM_TOUCH_PROBE`/`GAGGIMATE_SIM`-only Fixture category with 11 info rows, an enter/commit counter and one integer draft value.
- LVGL 8.4 pointer events on a pressed object: `LV_EVENT_PRESSED` at touch-down, `LV_EVENT_LONG_PRESSED` 400 ms later (`LV_INDEV_DEF_LONG_PRESS_TIME`), `LV_EVENT_LONG_PRESSED_REPEAT` every 100 ms after that (`LV_INDEV_DEF_LONG_PRESS_REP_TIME`), `LV_EVENT_RELEASED` at lift, `LV_EVENT_CLICKED` after a release with no drag (also after a long hold), `LV_EVENT_PRESS_LOST` if the pointer leaves the object; `lv_conf.h` does not override the timings. Hit testing: `lv_indev_search_obj` visits children before the parent, `lv_obj_hit_test` honours each object's own disabled state, so disabling a row does not disable its children.
- Icons: `img_plus_small_40x40`, `img_minus_small_40x40`, `img_angle_left_40x40`, `img_angle_right_40x40`, `img_check_40x40` in `eez/images.h`, recoloured with `lv_obj_set_style_img_recolor(_opa)`; `LV_SYMBOL_*` glyphs are in the Montserrat fonts. Pressed feedback from `DefaultUI::applyPressedFeedback` covers `lv_imgbtn`, clickable `lv_img`, and `lv_btn` whose background opacity is at least 20 percent; transparent text rows get nothing from it and must style their own `LV_STATE_PRESSED` text/image colour.
- Row text: a 320 px row with two 56 px controls leaves about 200 px for label and value; values such as "Argentina/Buenos Aires" in Montserrat 20 are around 240 px wide, so a one-line layout cannot hold every label and value.
- Touch targets are audited with `tools/touchmap.py` (effective hit rect = coords grown by the ext click pad, clipped by ancestors without `LV_OBJ_FLAG_OVERFLOW_VISIBLE`; padding a button inside a tight row container gains nothing unless the row has that flag, see `applyClickArea` in `eez/actions.cpp`).

## Scope
Files: `src/display/ui/default/settings/SettingsRows.h`, `src/display/ui/default/settings/SettingsRows.cpp`, and the Fixture category content in `src/display/ui/default/settings/SettingsUI.cpp` (or a `SettingsFixture.cpp` beside it).

## Requirements
- Common: each row is created with `lv_obj_t *row = settingsRow*Create(parent, "Label", const SettingsDebugTag *tags, user)`, fills the 320x56 slot, has `bg_opa` 0, and carries its label as a direct child (Montserrat 18) and its value as a direct child (Montserrat 20), laid out as two lines (label above value at the left) when the value plus controls would not fit one line, with `LV_LABEL_LONG_DOT` truncation as the last resort; `settingsRowSetValue` copies the canonical string into row-owned storage (bounded, PSRAM or a fixed buffer) and the value tag's `text` points at it, because LVGL writes the dots into the label's own buffer and `lv_label_get_text` returns them. Each row exposes `settingsRowSetValue(row, const char *)`, `settingsRowSetEnabled(row, bool)` (dims text and icons, disables every interactive descendant, cancels pending holds; re-enabling never resumes a hold) and the user pointer, which callbacks receive. Row, value and every control get their debug tags.
- Stepper: minus and plus `lv_imgbtn` controls at the right; callback `onStep(user, int dir, bool fast)` once on `LV_EVENT_PRESSED` and once per `LV_EVENT_LONG_PRESSED_REPEAT` while held, never on `LV_EVENT_CLICKED`; `fast` becomes true after 2 s of continuous hold measured from `PRESSED`; `RELEASED`, `PRESS_LOST`, disable, page removal and deletion end the hold. Hold and progress state (elapsed time, fast flag, unlock and confirm progress) is derived only from the events LVGL delivers to the row object; a free-standing `lv_timer` holding a row pointer is not acceptable (LVGL's `obj_del_core` resets the indev but delivers no cancel event, so such a timer would dangle after a page rebuild mid-hold). Each button's effective hit rectangle is at least 56x56 px and the two do not overlap.
- Choice: `<` and `>` arrows around the value; callback `onCycle(user, int dir)` with the same press-and-repeat protocol (no fast flag). Same target rules.
- Toggle: the whole row is the target (row object clickable, children not); the value shows "On"/"Off"; callback `onToggle(user, bool)` on `LV_EVENT_CLICKED`. Pressed state visibly changes the text colour.
- Action: whole-row target, optional value, callback `onActivate(user)` once per completed tap (`LV_EVENT_CLICKED`), used for navigation rows (Schedules, a schedule entry, Add schedule).
- Locked: wraps a stepper. Locked state hides the buttons and shows a lock glyph (`LV_SYMBOL_EYE_CLOSE` or `LV_SYMBOL_WARNING` is acceptable) and "hold to unlock"; pressing the row for 1 s (measured from `PRESSED`, progress shown, for example a growing underline) unlocks, reveals the buttons and consumes the current press until release so the unlocking press cannot step; releasing earlier cancels; `settingsRowSetLocked(row, bool)` relocks; callback `onUnlocked(user)`.
- Confirm: whole-row target; holding 2 s with visible progress calls `onConfirm(user)` once; release before that cancels and resets; disabled rows ignore the hold.
- Info: label and value only, not clickable, no controls.

title: Add the synthetic tap route: TouchInject module with LVGL and SDL hooks, /api/debug/tap
description:

title: Implement the Temperatures & timing category (offset, pressure rating, delays, auto-adjust)
description:
Implement the Temperatures & timing category: temperature offset and pressure sensor rating behind hold-to-unlock, brew and grind delay steppers, and the delay auto-adjust toggle, all saved when the category is left and reaching the controller board the way the web UI's save does.

## Context
- Fields (`src/display/core/Settings.h`): `temperatureOffset` (int C, `setTemperatureOffset`), `pressureScaling` (float bar, `setPressureScaling`), `brewDelay`/`grindDelay` (double ms, `setBrewDelay`/`setGrindDelay`, both clamped to 0..4000 by the setter), `delayAdjust` (bool, `setDelayAdjust`).
- How the controller board learns about them: the boiler setpoint is `target + temperatureOffset`, computed in `Controller::updateControl` and sent in the next control batch whenever it changes, so a new offset reaches the board on the next `loopLogic` pass with no call needed; the web save additionally calls `controller->setTargetTemp(controller->getTargetTemp())`, which assigns the current mode's target back to itself, calls `updateLastAction()` and re-emits the `boiler:targetTemperature:change` event; none of that is needed to propagate an offset. `Controller::setPressureScale()` (public) sends the pressure scaling when the board reports the pressure capability. Delays are read when a process starts. `Controller::loopLogic` writes `brewDelay`/`grindDelay` itself after a shot when `delayAdjust` is on, and can still be finishing that after the UI has returned to the menu, so `commit` must write only fields the user touched.
- The Fixture and placeholder rows, the row widgets, model and shell are described below.

## Scope
Files: `src/display/ui/default/settings/CatTemps.cpp` (defines `kCatTemps`), `tools/settings_ui_tests/test_temps.py`. `Controller.cpp` is not edited: the shell bead already wraps `loopLogic`'s delay auto-adjust writes in `Settings::Guard`.

## Requirements

One page. Title "Temperatures & timing", icon `img_thermometer_half_40x40`.
- All five deferred: edits go to the draft with touched flags; `commit` writes touched fields, calls `setPressureScale()` if the rating was written, logs `SettingsTemps: committed offset=%d scaling=%.1f brew=%d grind=%d adjust=%d` naming only the written fields, then triggers `settings:changed` if anything was written.
- `enter` relocks both locked rows; leaving and re-entering shows them locked again.
- Display formats from the model ("-3 C", "16.0 bar", "800 ms").

- [ ] Simulator (then loadtest device with `synth(0)`), via `settingsui(cat=0)` and taps: the five rows show the current values parsed from GET `/api/settings` (`temperatureOffset`, `pressureScaling`, `brewDelay`, `grindDelay`, `delayAdjust`), read through the dump's `Temperature offset/value` and sibling tags.
- [ ] A tap on the offset row's plus does nothing while locked; a 1200 ms press on the row unlocks it and does not step; a plus tap then shows the value +1; `/api/settings` still shows the old value until `settingsui(pop=1)`, after which it shows the new one within 6 s and the log has one `SettingsTemps: committed offset=` line.

- Activity: every touch inside settings calls `controller->updateLastAction()` so the standby timeout (`Controller::loopLogic`: `now > lastAction + settings.getStandbyTimeout()`, on the logic task on the device and in the one main loop on the simulator) does not fire mid-edit.
- Memory: immutable lookup tables are `const` PODs in flash (a `const std::vector` or `String` is not); runtime drafts, strings and callback contexts are small, bounded and owned by the shell for the life of the cover; anything sizeable goes to PSRAM; settings code never touches the animation hot slab (`bganim::allocHot`). LVGL objects allocate from PSRAM through `gm_lv_malloc`, so widget count is not an internal-DRAM concern, but plain C++ allocations are, and `/api/debug/heap` (`int_free`, `dma_free`) is read with the largest page and draft open.
- Wire format of GET `/api/settings` (the oracle for what was written): `standbyTimeout` and `standbyBrightnessTimeout` are in seconds (stored in ms), `temperatureOffset` and `pressureScaling` are numeric strings, `bgAnimPlateColor` and `elementTintColor` are `#rrggbb` strings, `startupMode` is `standby` or `brew`, `autowakeupSchedules` is `HH:MM|ddddddd;...` (Mon..Sun). Scripts parse before comparing.
- Verification venue: the desktop simulator first (`pio run -e display-sim`, `SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy GM_SIM_PORT=<port> ./.pio/build/display-sim/program`, web server on `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` (8080 by default), state under `sim_data/` in the working directory; the build is repaired by gm-bzu.9), the bench device second (`display-loadtest` build at 192.168.1.121). The simulator runs the LVGL UI, Settings, the web server and the debug routes on one cooperative thread with no panel and no background animation renderer (`SleepAnimation` is a stub under `GAGGIMATE_SIM` and `updateState` skips animation and plate application): it verifies navigation, interaction, values, persistence and theme colours. Animation frame counters, the applied frame-rate cap, rendered gradients, plate pixels, memory and frame-rate numbers are device-only, and a simulator pass says nothing about the device's concurrency (TouchInject's critical section and the Settings lock are reviewed on their own merits). Build note: a new or deleted source file under `src/` needs `touch src/CMakeLists.txt` before the ESP-IDF envs pick it up (the glob has no CONFIGURE_DEPENDS); when a symbol's provenance matters, check the ELF with the toolchain's `nm` (`~/.platformio/packages/toolchain-xtensa-esp-elf/bin/xtensa-esp32s3-elf-nm`).
- Rules: never POST `/api/settings` by hand (the web UI is the only safe writer) and never print the `wifiPassword` field of GET `/api/settings`; scripts read it through a filter that drops that key. No em dashes or double hyphens in prose, comments or commit messages.

title: UI responsiveness: faster touch feedback and overlay refresh
description: Cut the time from a touch to the pixels changing on the panel, and raise the LVGL overlay refresh rate, without touching the hardware or DRAM invariants in CLAUDE.md. Baseline (bench board, 2026-09-06, scratch ui_baseline_2026-09-06.md): press to overlay publish median 55 ms, p90 78; release median 70 ms, p90 336 (page changes); pass avg 49 ms, snapshot avg 72 ms. Plan from two oracle reports (GPT-6 Astra and Fable), both agreeing on order: measure PSRAM contention share, read touch input between snapshot clips, cache the meter tick ring, repair the back overlay buffer by copy instead of a second render. Every step is measured on the board with GM_UISTAT/GM_TOUCHLAT over serial against the baseline.

title: Measure the animation's share of UI pass time (contention A/B)
description: Run the press probe and a 90 s serial capture twice on the board: animation loop at 5 fps and at the stored 45 fps, same taps. Compare GM_UISTAT pass, snapshot and publish averages and GM_TOUCHLAT medians. Outcome: a number for how much of the LVGL pass is PSRAM bus contention from the render task versus LVGL's own draw work. Decides whether any render-task work (GDMA refill, priority) is worth doing. Acceptance: both captures on disk in C:\work\camshots, the two tables in the scratch baseline file, and a one-line conclusion in the bead.
close_reason: Done. Bench board, display-loadtest 754e4b14, animation 13, press probe, 110 s captures (C:\work\camshots\uistat_qo3_fps45.log and uistat_qo3_fps5.log): cap 45 vs cap 5 per refresh: snapshot 55.9 vs 38.7 ms, draw 42.3 vs 29.0, clear 10.2 vs 7.3, scan 13.1 vs 10.0, scrim 11.9 vs 6.3, publish 25.2 vs 16.4; release p90 404 vs 204 ms. Conclusion: the render task's PSRAM traffic at cap 45 costs a UI pass about 30 percent (up to 50 on the PSRAM-bound scrim rebuild). Render-side work is worth doing but the UI side is still the larger part.

title: Read touch input between overlay snapshot clips
description: DefaultUI::refreshSleepOverlay snapshots every owed clip and publishes once; a touch that lands during a long multi-clip pass waits for all of them. Change: run lv_task_handler (input read plus timers) between clips when more than one clip is owed and the pass has already run past a budget (about 30 ms), publishing once at the end. Also make sure the UI loop reads input before it starts a snapshot pass. No visual change. Acceptance: GM_TOUCHLAT press median and p90 on the board do not get worse than the baseline (55 / 78 ms) and release p90 falls from 336 ms; the settings runner (tools/settings_ui_test.py) passes on device; no new full-screen snapshots per GM_UISTAT area.

title: Cache the meter tick ring instead of redrawing every tick
description: action_on_meter_draw (src/display/ui/default/eez/actions.cpp) draws each visible scale tick as a round-capped lv_draw_line: four masks plus two circle rects per tick, about 2 ms per tick, 14 to 20 ticks per refresh, the largest item inside the ~100 ms redraw. Change: render the tick ring once into an RGB565+A8 image in PSRAM (lv_canvas or a hand-built lv_img_dsc_t), blit it with lv_draw_img, and rebuild only the ticks whose colour changed when the value moves. Pixel output must match the current look (round caps kept). Acceptance: /api/debug/fb of the brew and steam screens matches before/after within dither noise for the ring; GM_UISTAT snapshot avg on the temps screen falls by at least 20 ms against the baseline (72 ms); no new heap allocation on the internal pool (check /api/debug/heap dma_free before and after); dial value changes still redraw sector-sized (CLAUDE.md meter invariant).
close_reason: Done in 7500c75c. Sim brew/steam/water framebuffers before vs after: 180 of 230400 px differ by at most one RGB565 step (cap-over-body double mix). Board: meter time per refresh 18.5 to 7.8 ms, draw 55.2 to 42.3, snapshot 65.9 to 55.9 (target was 20 ms off the snapshot; got 10, the rest is the per-pixel alpha composite into PSRAM). dma_free 38.7 KB after vs 36.3 KB before, no internal allocation; cache is 122 KB PSRAM plus 208 B static. Codex compared the board captures and saw no tick difference.

title: Repair the back overlay buffer by copying from the front buffer
description: The overlay is double-buffered and every dirty rect is owed to both buffers, so each change is rendered twice through LVGL (once per buffer, on consecutive passes). Change: when the back buffer owes rects the front buffer already holds, copy those rects (RGB565 and A8) from the front buffer instead of rendering them again; only rects dirtied since the front's last publish need a render. Acceptance: GM_UISTAT snapshot area per 5 s window on the temps screen roughly halves against baseline for the same telemetry updates; framebuffer check via /api/debug/fb shows no stale content after ten value changes; runner passes on device.

title: Interlaced frames: invalidate the destination cache for regionally warmed bands too
description: In SleepAnimation::renderFrame the direct GDMA path invalidates the destination cache lines (esp_cache_msync M2C) only for bands with bandInterlaced true (around line 4159). A band under regional warm-up (bandWarm > 0) in an otherwise interlaced frame has bandInterlaced false, is written whole by GDMA, and the frame never flips, so presentFrame's whole-buffer invalidate does not run either. The bounce refill can then read stale cache lines for those rows until eviction. Flagged by the GPT-6 Astra oracle (2026-09-06); hidden today by streaming eviction. Fix: key the invalidate on the frame being interlaced (no flip coming), not on the band, and cover the whole band region when it was pushed as one transfer. Acceptance: tear_checked/tear_live on /api/debug/anim unchanged over a 5 minute soak with the settings runner driving overlay updates; no new msync_fail; band_us unchanged within noise.
